items.followUp: Name and describe four other branches of Chemistry.

rubric.why: A branch earns credit when it is named and its subject is correctly described.
rubric.description: Names physical chemistry and describes its subject.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct branch and a suitable description.

rubric.why: Organic chemistry is correctly identified by its study of carbon compounds.
rubric.description: Names organic chemistry and describes its subject.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct branch and a suitable description.

rubric.why: Inorganic chemistry is correctly identified by its study of elements and their compounds.
rubric.description: Names inorganic chemistry and describes its subject.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct branch and a suitable description.

rubric.why: Biochemistry concerns chemical substances and reactions in living organisms.
rubric.description: Names biochemistry and describes its subject.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct branch and a suitable description.

modelAnswer: Physical chemistry deals with the laws and principles governing the properties and behaviour of matter.
Organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
Inorganic chemistry deals with the properties and reactions of elements and their compounds, except most carbon compounds.
Biochemistry deals with the chemical substances and reactions occurring in living organisms.

items.followUp: Explain why water molecules attract one another through hydrogen bonding.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding is an intermolecular force of attraction.
rubric.description: Identifies hydrogen bonding as an intermolecular force.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for identifying it as an intermolecular force.

rubric.why: The hydrogen atom must be bonded to a highly electronegative atom.
rubric.description: States the condition for hydrogen bonding: hydrogen is bonded to a highly electronegative atom.

rubric.why: Oxygen, nitrogen and fluorine are examples of highly electronegative atoms involved in hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of a highly electronegative atom involved in hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for naming a correct example such as oxygen, nitrogen or fluorine.

rubric.why: The hydrogen is attracted to an electronegative atom in a neighbouring molecule.
rubric.description: Explains the attraction between hydrogen and an electronegative atom on a neighbouring molecule.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for describing this neighbouring-molecule attraction.

rubric.why: Water is a valid example of molecules that form hydrogen bonds.
rubric.description: Gives water as an example of hydrogen bonding between molecules.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for a correct example such as water.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding is a special intermolecular force of attraction between molecules.
It occurs when a hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom, such as oxygen, nitrogen or fluorine, is attracted to an electronegative atom in a neighbouring molecule.
The attraction is between molecules and is weaker than the covalent bond within each molecule.
Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another.
Hydrogen bonding helps account for water's unusually high boiling point compared with similar small molecules.

items.followUp: State four physical properties of metals and non-metals.

rubric.why: Lustre is a standard contrasting physical property of metals and non-metals.
rubric.description: States that metals are generally lustrous and non-metals generally dull.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Malleability of metals contrasts with the brittleness of solid non-metals.
rubric.description: States that metals are generally malleable and solid non-metals generally brittle.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Conductivity is a key physical difference between the two groups.
rubric.description: States that metals generally conduct heat and electricity well, while non-metals generally conduct them poorly.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Sonority is another standard physical property of metals.
rubric.description: States that metals are generally sonorous and non-metals generally non-sonorous.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct contrast.

modelAnswer: Metals are generally lustrous, whereas non-metals are generally dull.
Metals are generally malleable and ductile, whereas solid non-metals are generally brittle.
Metals are generally good conductors of heat and electricity, whereas non-metals are generally poor conductors.
Metals are generally sonorous, whereas non-metals are generally non-sonorous.

items.followUp: The empirical formula of a compound is CH₂ and its molar mass is 42 g mol⁻¹. Find its molecular formula.

rubric.why: The molecular formula represents the actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule.
rubric.description: Defines a molecular formula in terms of the actual number of each type of atom in a molecule.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The empirical formula is multiplied by n, calculated from the molecular mass divided by the empirical formula mass.
rubric.description: States how to derive the molecular formula from the empirical formula and gives the multiplier relationship.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the multiplier method and the correct expression for n.

modelAnswer: The molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule of a compound.
It is derived from the empirical formula by multiplying all its subscripts by n, where n = molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass.

items.followUp: Define one atomic mass unit and state its value in grams.

rubric.why: The atomic mass unit is defined relative to a carbon-12 atom.
rubric.description: Defines one atomic mass unit as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for the carbon-12 definition.

rubric.why: This is the accepted approximate value of one atomic mass unit in grams.
rubric.description: States the value of one atomic mass unit in grams.
rubric.how: Give 1 mark for 1.66 × 10⁻²⁴ g or an equivalent notation.

modelAnswer: One atomic mass unit (u) is one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
